question: does the density crop change the delivered surface at the shipped defaults, or does the support crop remove everything it removes?
input: o3d.data.DemoICPPointClouds, fused and downsampled at voxel 0.05

at_the_shipped_defaults.so: none of the density crop's removals would have survived the support crop, so the published removal count describes work the next stage was going to do. The count is not wrong; reading it as this filter's effect on the delivered surface is

control_support_cropping_disabled.so: the crop and this measurement both work. What the shipped configuration shows is overlap with the next filter, not an inert filter

is_the_density_crop_selective.so: the crop is strongly selective -- its removals sit far from any observed point -- which is the reason it duplicates the support crop rather than a reason to distrust it

how_stable_are_these_figures.why_this_is_here: an independent lane reproduced every structural result here and found 31 figures moving in the fourth significant digit, including between its own two runs. Poisson reconstruction is not deterministic and nothing seeds it
how_stable_are_these_figures.repeated_as: separate solves in one interpreter, because the variation is per-solve: repeated calls spread as widely as separate processes did

the_margin_the_assertions_have.figure: triangles removed at quantile 0.20 and the shipped support distance, the row the grid assertion is scoped to

how_stable_are_these_figures.so: every quantity this record's argument rests on is identical in every repeat: how many vertices the density crop removes, how many of those the support crop would have removed anyway, whether the delivered mesh is unchanged, and whether the control can see the crop at all. What moves is triangle counts and surface areas, by less than half a percent. Those are reported because they are what a mesh measurement looks like, not because any conclusion needs their digits -- the figures elsewhere in this record are one draw from this spread, and a reader comparing a regeneration should expect the same scale of difference

what_this_does_not_claim.not_that_the_density_crop_is_wrong: it removes extrapolated surface and does it well. The claim is about what its published removal count tells a reader when the support crop also runs
what_this_does_not_claim.not_that_it_should_be_removed: with support cropping disabled it is the only filter and it works. Changing a default is a separate decision from reporting honestly
what_this_does_not_claim.not_a_general_result_about_every_scan: one real scan and the pipeline's synthetic fragments, both of which show the same complete overlap at the defaults. A capture whose low-density regions sit close to observed points would behave differently, and the published contribution would show it
